articles.title: SolidJob
articles.excerpt: We are told that to scale Ruby background workloads across multiple CPU cores, we have two choices: process forking (e.g., Pitchfork) which incurs massive Copy-on-Write memory overhead and risk of OOM…
articles.body: We are told that to scale Ruby background workloads across multiple CPU cores, we have two choices: process forking (e.g., Pitchfork) which incurs massive Copy-on-Write memory overhead and risk of OOM kills under load, or database-backed queues (e.g., Solid Queue) which introduce heavy synchronous disk I/O and row-locking bottlenecks [1.8, 1.10]. To break this cycle, I built SolidJobs (v0.5.0): an open-source, Ractor-local Redis task runtime engineered from scratch around a strict shared-nothing architecture [1.8]. The Architecture: Warm IPC Pool over Unix Sockets Instead of forcing workers to share mutable application states, SolidJobs completely isolates concurrency multiplexing at the OS kernel level [1.8, 1.10].

articles.title: Open weights don't make a 1T model cheap to run
articles.excerpt: Mistral Large 4 is 1.05T parameters with 52B active per token. The 52B sets your compute. The 1T sets your memory, because every expert has to stay resident in GPU memory for the router to pick it. At…
articles.body: Mistral Large 4 is 1.05T parameters with 52B active per token. The 52B sets your compute. The 1T sets your memory, because every expert has to stay resident in GPU memory for the router to pick it. At FP8 that is about a terabyte of weights before any KV cache. That makes 8x B200 (1,440 GB) the first single node I'd plan FP8 on. Rented at about $53.52 an hour, it has to sustain roughly 7,100 output tokens per second all month to beat Mistral's preview API price, about 3,600 at list price. Most teams won't have that concurrency. My read: the open weights matter most as an option that caps vendor leverage. Running them yourself pays off only for organisations that already run GPU clusters.

One attempt holds the candidate's answers and, where the exercise has written items, the full AI review of them, both as jsonb . Those columns are the point of the table and they are also the reason you cannot write the obvious query. select * ... where user_id = $1 limit 100 to render a hundred one-line rows means moving every word anyone typed into that page's memory to find out whether to print 72 or Not scored . articles.title: What a Supabase database backup leaves out
articles.excerpt: A Supabase database backup restores your Postgres data. Most projects depend on more than that, and the gaps only show up when you restore into a new project. Here is what does not come back from the…
articles.body: A Supabase database backup restores your Postgres data. Most projects depend on more than that, and the gaps only show up when you restore into a new project. Here is what does not come back from the database backup alone. What Where it lives In the database backup? Tables, rows, RLS policies, functions Postgres Yes Auth users auth schema in Postgres Yes, if you back up that schema Storage file contents Object storage No, only the metadata rows Edge Function code Deployed separately No Edge Function secrets Project settings No Passwords of custom database roles Postgres roles Need to be reset after a restore Storage files The storage.objects table tells you which files exist. The files themselves are not in it. After a restore the app can list every file and download none of them.

articles.body: 一句話結論：用 k3d 可以在一台機器上用 Docker 容器模擬多節點的 Kubernetes，但要記得兩件事： PV 的資料要掛到主機上 ，還有 k3s 本來就內建 local-path-provisioner，不要再裝一套 。 遇到的問題 需求很單純：一個可以隨便玩、隨便砍、但資料不會跟著消失的 Kubernetes 環境。 放在自己的機器上，不用每個月付雲端的錢。 最省事的選擇其實是 minikube 或 kind。 但我這次要的是 多節點 ，想試 Pod 排程、節點故障這些行為，而且要接近真實的 k3s。 k3d 剛好符合：它把 k3s 包在 Docker 容器裡，一個容器就是一個節點，建一個 3 節點叢集大概一分鐘。 這篇從一台乾淨的 Ubuntu 開始，走完整個建置過程，也會講到中間踩到的幾個坑。 手把手步驟 步驟一：裝 Docker k3d 的節點是 Docker 容器，所以 Docker 是第一個要裝的。 用 Docker 官方的 apt 套件庫來裝（不是 Ubuntu 預設套件庫裡那個舊版）： sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl sudo install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings sudo curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.sources << EOF Types: deb URIs: https://downlo…

articles.title: Fridge hack costing millions and sparking fires stemmed from poor security
articles.excerpt: Incident hitting 700 supermarkets exploited outdated devices exposed to the Internet.
articles.body: Earlier this week, a mass hack of refrigeration systems at an estimated 700 supermarkets throughout France caused them to suddenly malfunction, causing spoilage of untold tons of perishables and, in some cases, fires. As is now the norm, basic cybersecurity would have prevented it. French authorities say the systems, made up of entire fleets of refrigerators and freezers throughout a store, were hacked. More specifically, Internet-connected controllers that allow technicians to remotely administer the store-wide systems were compromised. The unknown attackers responsible then activated defrosters long enough for the fridges to reach temperatures as high as 50° Celsius (122° Fahrenheit).

articles.title: Planetary genealogy: Milky Way worlds belong to 1 of 2 ‘families,’ scientists find
articles.excerpt: Scientists have performed a cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems.
articles.body: You can tell a lot about how a child will age by looking at their parents, and it turns out that this could be true for planetary systems, too. Scientists have performed cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems. The study team, led by researchers at the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), studied 300 of the best-understood multiplanet systems of the over 1,000 that astronomers have discovered in the Milky Way. The team's research clarifies how the environments around infant stars directly affect planetary fates and, in turn, the survival of extrasolar planets, or exoplanets , that are potentially capable of hosting life.

articles.excerpt: "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
articles.body: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet of Things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered.
